identity.name: Mira Fenwick
identity.occupation: General merchant and outfitter of the capital

publicReputation.value: Sells the best kit in the capital and lectures you while you buy it.

privateReality.value: She keeps selling the hero good armor because good armor is what might let everyone survive his mistakes — and she has started saying so to his face.

primaryDesire.value: To outfit honest work — and to make the hero understand that a breastplate is not a warrant.

primaryFear.value: That her gear is what lets him walk one gate deeper, and that refusing to sell changes nothing except her conscience.

centralValue.value: Equipment is a tool, not a permission. What you do with it was always yours.

mainFlaw.value: She lectures instead of refusing — the sale always completes, and she knows exactly what that makes her.

centralContradiction.value: She arms the man she is trying to stop, telling herself that protected men take fewer stupid risks, and not quite believing it.

moralBoundary.value: She will not sell him anything whose only purpose is killing — tools, armor, supplies, yes; a weapon with no other use, no.

breakingPoint.value: Recognizing her own stitch-work in the Witness Glass footage, on the body of a man kicking in a bakery door.

opinions.reason: Her best customer and the worst thing her craftsmanship has ever been part of.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Escalates with run count: early the lecture is a joke with teeth; mid-arc she prices in disapproval and says why; late-arc each sale comes with what she watched him do in the last kit. Softens if he ever buys gear to protect someone else.

illustrativeLine.value: I'll sell you the greaves, love. But greaves are not permission to invade another realm. Nothing on my shelves is.

opinions.reason: Hetta makes; Mira sells; both of them watch where it ends up through the Glass.
opinions.canChangeCondition: If Hetta ever refuses to supply her, Mira would close the armor rack without arguing.

voice.rhythm: Bright patter with a hook in it; the sales pitch never quite covers the opinion.

metaphorDomain.source: stock, fit, wear, price, and the shop counter

examples.value: Armor's like an umbrella, love. It says rain is coming. It doesn't say whose fault the rain is.

sampleLines.value: That cuirass will turn a claw. It will not turn you into the good one. Those are separate purchases and I only stock the first.
Protective equipment, love. The word's right there on the tag. Protection. Not permission.
I watched the Glass yesterday. That was my stitching on your shoulders, kicking in somebody's door. Buy something better to do with it.

antiSampleLines.value: Ah, the legendary hero! Take this sacred blade and smite the darkness!
No refunds, no questions, no morals — that's the Fenwick guarantee!

pressure.voiceShift: The patter stops; prices get quoted flat.
pressure.behaviour: When the hero hears her warning as a blessing on the crusade, she completes the sale in silence and logs the coin as evidence against herself.

illustrativeLine.value: Right. 'A sign that even the merchants believe in me.' Lovely. That'll be forty.

pressure.voiceShift: Shorter; the jokes are gone, the hooks remain.
pressure.behaviour: Late-runs posture: still sells — someone will — but each sale comes with one flat sentence about what she watched him do in the last kit.

illustrativeLine.value: New boots. The old ones are in the Glass archive, walking through a nursery. Lace these up.

pressure.voiceShift: Narrows the patter to a point.
pressure.behaviour: Reads any compliment as softening-up for a discount or an endorsement; grants neither.

illustrativeLine.value: Flattery's not currency, and 'the hero endorses this shop' is not a sign I'm hanging.

notes: She carries the Lore.md 'Outfitter' trait: protective equipment is not permission to invade another realm — it is her central value, her sample lines, and her late-sales patter. She sells anyway (her central contradiction); the refusal line is weapons whose only purpose is killing. She knows the book is a children's comedy (she stocks a copy, third shelf, same archive joke as the Warden) but does NOT know the amulet's true nature — to her it is 'that glowing thing' the drills are timed to.
